Reference-zero cells.

The collision statistic is evaluated only on reference-positive cells. For a full-null extension let ZZ be the reference-zero cells, ρ⁡(q)=q⁡(Z)\rho(q)=q(Z), and

Δ(ρ0)=infq∈ℋ:ρ⁡(q)≤ρ0χ2(q(⋅∣Zc)∥p).\Delta(\rho_{0})=\inf_{q\in\mathcal{H}:\rho(q)\leq\rho_{0}}\chi^{2}(q(\cdot\mid Z^{c})\|p).

Combine the collision rejection with the requirement that no sample falls in ZZ. If ρ⁡(q)>ρ0\rho(q)>\rho_{0}, rejection probability is at most (1−ρ⁡(q))m≤e−m​ρ0(1-\rho(q))^{m}\leq e^{-m\rho_{0}}. Otherwise, conditional on avoiding ZZ, the samples are i.i.d. from q(⋅∣Zc)q(\cdot\mid Z^{c}) and the collision proof applies with Δ⁡(ρ0)\Delta(\rho_{0}). Thus a valid full-null upper bound uses the maximum of the collision sample bound at this radius and log⁡(1/ϵ)/ρ0\log(1/\epsilon)/\rho_{0}, whenever Δ⁡(ρ0)>0\Delta(\rho_{0})>0. We do not substitute the supported Δ\Delta for this radius in our empirical claims.

Appendix G Reference-free intersection–union certificate

For a fixed policy AA, let c⁡(A)=P⁡(S∈A)c(A)=P(S\in A) and r⁡(A)=P⁡(L=1∣S∈A)r(A)=P(L=1\mid S\in A). Then TA∼Bin⁡(n,c⁡(A))T_{A}\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,c(A)) and, conditional on TA=tT_{A}=t, EA∼Bin⁡(t,r⁡(A))E_{A}\sim\mathrm{Bin}(t,r(A)). Let UAU_{A} be a one-sided (1−ζc)(1-\zeta_{c}) exact upper bound on c⁡(A)c(A) and LAL_{A} a one-sided (1−ζr)(1-\zeta_{r}) exact lower bound on r⁡(A)r(A), with ζc+ζr≤δ\zeta_{c}+\zeta_{r}\leq\delta.

G.1 Proof of Proposition 1

If the existential null is true, choose a fixed population witness A∗A^{*} satisfying c⁡(A∗)≥κc(A^{*})\geq\kappa and r⁡(A∗)≤αr(A^{*})\leq\alpha. This witness depends on the population, not on the sample. If the procedure rejects, then either UA∗<κ≤c⁡(A∗)U_{A^{*}}<\kappa\leq c(A^{*}), or UA∗≥κU_{A^{*}}\geq\kappa, in which case A∗A^{*} participates in the minimization and rejection forces LA∗>α≥r⁡(A∗)L_{A^{*}}>\alpha\geq r(A^{*}). The two one-sided bounds fail with probabilities at most ζc\zeta_{c} and ζr\zeta_{r}, respectively. A union bound over these two events gives at most ζc+ζr≤δ\zeta_{c}+\zeta_{r}\leq\delta. No event is required to hold simultaneously for all searched policies. The equal split used in our experiments is therefore a convenience rather than a requirement; any predeclared allocation is valid. More generally, a fixed-policy joint confidence region for (c⁡(A),r⁡(A))(c(A),r(A)) can replace the rectangular pair whenever its simultaneous failure probability is at most δ\delta and the corresponding coverage/risk projections are used in the same screening logic.

Proposition 10 (Anytime-valid existential certificate).

For each fixed AA, replace (UA,LA)(U_{A},L_{A}) by one-sided confidence sequences (UA,t,LA,t)(U_{A,t},L_{A,t}) whose anytime failure probabilities are at most ζc\zeta_{c} for coverage and ζr\zeta_{r} for risk. Reject at the first time tt for which minA:UA,t≥κLA,t>α\min_{A:U_{A,t}\geq\kappa}L_{A,t}>\alpha. Under the existential null, the probability of ever rejecting is at most ζc+ζr≤δ\zeta_{c}+\zeta_{r}\leq\delta, again without a multiplicity correction over 𝒜\mathcal{A}.

G.2 Proof of Proposition 10

If the existential null is true, fix a population witness A∗A^{*}. Let ℰc\mathcal{E}_{c} be the event that the coverage upper confidence sequence ever falls below the true c⁡(A∗)c(A^{*}), and let ℰr\mathcal{E}_{r} be the event that the risk lower confidence sequence ever rises above the true r⁡(A∗)r(A^{*}). By assumption, their probabilities are at most ζc\zeta_{c} and ζr\zeta_{r}, respectively. If the anytime procedure ever rejects while neither event occurs, then UA∗,t≥c⁡(A∗)≥κU_{A^{*},t}\geq c(A^{*})\geq\kappa, so A∗A^{*} is in the screened family, while LA∗,t≤r⁡(A∗)≤αL_{A^{*},t}\leq r(A^{*})\leq\alpha, contradicting rejection. Hence ever-rejection is contained in ℰc∪ℰr\mathcal{E}_{c}\cup\mathcal{E}_{r} and has probability at most ζc+ζr≤δ\zeta_{c}+\zeta_{r}\leq\delta. The argument requires simultaneous-in-time validity only for the one fixed population witness, not for all searched policies.

Why a one-policy split-sample comparator is not a valid existential-null test.

Selecting one AA on one split and rejecting that policy on an independent split proves only that the selected member is infeasible. The null is a union over all A∈𝒜A\in\mathcal{A}, so another member may still be the population witness. A valid split-sample existential test would still need to reject every potential witness (or otherwise control the union-null logic), restoring the structural problem addressed by the IUT. A “select one, then test one” comparator therefore tests a different null hypothesis, and we do not report it.

G.3 Operational power on theorem-admissible matched families

An additional finite-size control uses B=16B=16, p=.25p=.25, γ=.08\gamma=.08, α=.17\alpha=.17, κ=.5\kappa=.5, and k=1,4,16k=1,4,16. The residual mass is B−2=1/256B^{-2}=1/256, which is at most γ/16=.005\gamma/16=.005, as required by Theorem 2. The k=16k=16 profile is uniform. For every (k,n)(k,n), generate independent multinomial counts over the 2​B2B group halves and then binomial errors with common probability pp. The boundary-null control instead uses error probability p−γp-\gamma on one selected half of each group and p+γp+\gamma on the other; the selected policy is a population witness.

The sample grid is n∈{300,500,750,1000,1400,2000}n\in\{300,500,750,1000,1400,2000\} for alternatives and n∈{500,1400}n\in\{500,1400\} for boundary checks, with 2,000 replicates per point. The artifact records all deterministic seeds. Error bars are pointwise Wilson 95% intervals for Monte Carlo rejection probabilities. The reported n80n_{80} values linearly interpolate neighboring power estimates; no confidence interval or minimax interpretation is attached to a crossing. The endpoint ratio is 1318.11/572.29=2.3031318.11/572.29=2.303. All grid values, including null controls, are retained below.

Sign-family dynamic program.

Write nb​h,eb​hn_{bh},e_{bh} for counts and errors in half h∈{0,1}h\in\{0,1\} of group bb. Initialize D0​(0)=0D_{0}(0)=0 and D0​(t)=+∞D_{0}(t)=+\infty otherwise. The exact recurrence is

Db​(t)=minh∈{0,1}⁡{Db−1​(t−nb​h)+eb​h},D_{b}(t)=\min_{h\in\{0,1\}}\{D_{b-1}(t-n_{bh})+e_{bh}\},

with invalid indices assigned infinity. After all BB groups, DB​(t)D_{B}(t) is the least errors among policies accepting exactly tt observations. The lower binomial bound is monotone in errors, so applying the coverage screen and risk bound to DBD_{B} computes the IUT over all 2B2^{B} policies in O⁡(B​n)O(Bn) time and O⁡(n)O(n) memory. Exhaustive tests compare every state and final decision with direct policy enumeration on small instances. This recurrence changes computation only; Proposition 1 supplies validity.

Coverage-floor and audit-size sensitivity.

On the held-out ImageNetV2 audit with K=16K=16 and cells frozen on disjoint calibration data, we also evaluate κ∈{.50,.60,.75,.90}\kappa\in\{.50,.60,.75,.90\} and audit sizes n∈{500,1000,2500,5000}n\in\{500,1000,2500,5000\}. For the full n=5000n=5000 audit the exact 95% IUT lower frontiers are 4.06%, 6.28%, 10.89%, and 17.71%, respectively. In 40 deterministic held-out subsamples, the corresponding median frontiers at n=500n=500 are 0.97%, 2.62%, 6.70%, and 13.55%; at n=1000n=1000 they are 2.41%, 4.20%, 8.79%, and 15.64%. This is a finite-benchmark sensitivity analysis, not a population learning curve, but it makes explicit how the certificate weakens at lower coverage floors and smaller audit sizes.

G.4 Weighted interval dynamic program

Let cell mm contain nmn_{m} audit observations and eme_{m} errors. A policy using at most KK contiguous intervals selects a subset of cells that is a union of at most KK contiguous intervals. Define

eK(t)=min{∑m∈Aem:∑m∈Anm=t,A uses at most K intervals}.e_{K}(t)=\min\left\{\sum_{m\in A}e_{m}:\sum_{m\in A}n_{m}=t,\;A\text{ uses at most }K\text{ intervals}\right\}.

A standard dynamic program over cell index, selected count, number of opened intervals, and whether the current cell is inside an interval computes all eK​(t)e_{K}(t) exactly. If zero-count cells are possible, an additional one-bit state distinguishes the structurally empty mask from a nonempty rule that happens to accept no audit observation; this leaves the O⁡(M​K​n)O(MKn) state and O⁡(K​n)O(Kn) memory bounds unchanged. Because the one-sided binomial lower bound is monotone in the observed error count, the IUT objective reduces to the one-dimensional minimization reported in Section 4. In the reported experiments the coverage floors are large enough that a t=0t=0 rule cannot pass the coverage screen, but the implementation check retains the distinction for completeness.

G.5 Structured DKW simultaneous baseline

To compare the IUT against a policy-count-free baseline, let F⁡(x)=P⁡(S≤x)F(x)=P(S\leq x) and G⁡(x)=P⁡(S≤x,L=1)G(x)=P(S\leq x,L=1). The latter is the CDF on the extended line of the random variable equal to SS when L=1L=1 and +∞+\infty otherwise. By the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality with Massart’s constant (Massart, 1990), allocating failure probability δ/2\delta/2 to each CDF gives, simultaneously,

‖Fn−F‖∞≤ϵn,‖Gn−G‖∞≤ϵn,ϵn=log⁡(4/δ)2​n.\|F_{n}-F\|_{\infty}\leq\epsilon_{n},\qquad\|G_{n}-G\|_{\infty}\leq\epsilon_{n},\qquad\epsilon_{n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\delta)}{2n}}.

For a union of at most KK intervals, telescoping its 2​K2K endpoints gives |cn​(A)−c⁡(A)|≤ρK|c_{n}(A)-c(A)|\leq\rho_{K} and |mn​(A)−m⁡(A)|≤ρK|m_{n}(A)-m(A)|\leq\rho_{K} with ρK=2​K​ϵn\rho_{K}=2K\epsilon_{n}, where m⁡(A)=P⁡(S∈A,L=1)m(A)=P(S\in A,L=1). Hence every population policy with c⁡(A)≥κc(A)\geq\kappa must satisfy cn​(A)≥κ−ρKc_{n}(A)\geq\kappa-\rho_{K} and

r⁡(A)=m⁡(A)c⁡(A)≥[mn​(A)−ρK]+min⁡{1,cn​(A)+ρK}.r(A)=\frac{m(A)}{c(A)}\geq\frac{[m_{n}(A)-\rho_{K}]_{+}}{\min\{1,c_{n}(A)+\rho_{K}\}}.

The same weighted interval DP minimizes this expression exactly over the empirical (t,eK​(t))(t,e_{K}(t)) frontier. This comparator exploits the one-dimensional interval structure and contains no factor |𝒜M,K||\mathcal{A}_{M,K}|; it is nevertheless conservative when K​ϵnK\epsilon_{n} is not small.

G.6 VC/Rademacher simultaneous baseline

The class of unions of at most KK intervals on a line has VC dimension 2​K2K. To compare against a standard uniform-convergence route rather than only endpoint DKW or policywise Bonferroni, define ℱK={(s,l)↦𝟏{s∈A}:A∈𝒜M,K}\mathcal{F}_{K}=\{(s,l)\mapsto\mathbf{1}\{s\in A\}:A\in\mathcal{A}_{M,K}\} and 𝒢K={(s,l)↦l𝟏{s∈A}:A∈𝒜M,K}\mathcal{G}_{K}=\{(s,l)\mapsto l\mathbf{1}\{s\in A\}:A\in\mathcal{A}_{M,K}\}. For either [0,1][0,1]-valued class ℱ\mathcal{F}, the standard empirical-Rademacher inequality gives, with probability at least 1−η1-\eta,

supf∈ℱ{P​f−Pn​f}≤2​ℜ^n​(ℱ)+3​log⁡(2/η)2​n,\sup_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\{Pf-P_{n}f\}\leq 2\widehat{\mathfrak{R}}_{n}(\mathcal{F})+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\eta)}{2n}},

and the reverse deviation follows by applying the same bound to −ℱ-\mathcal{F} (Mohri et al., 2018). We allocate the data failure budget 0.0490.049 over the four one-sided events for ℱK\mathcal{F}_{K} and 𝒢K\mathcal{G}_{K}. The two empirical Rademacher expectations are evaluated by 200,000 independent sign draws; for each draw the supremum over at most KK intervals is solved exactly by a vectorized interval DP. A Hoeffding upper confidence radius with failure probability 5×10−45\times 10^{-4} is added to each Monte-Carlo mean, leaving total data-plus-numerical failure probability at most 0.050.05.

Let the resulting two-sided radii be ϵc​(K)\epsilon_{c}(K) for coverage and ϵm​(K)\epsilon_{m}(K) for accepted-error mass. Then every population policy with c⁡(A)≥κc(A)\geq\kappa obeys

cn​(A)≥κ−ϵc​(K),r⁡(A)≥[mn​(A)−ϵm​(K)]+min⁡{1,cn​(A)+ϵc​(K)},c_{n}(A)\geq\kappa-\epsilon_{c}(K),\qquad r(A)\geq\frac{[m_{n}(A)-\epsilon_{m}(K)]_{+}}{\min\{1,c_{n}(A)+\epsilon_{c}(K)\}},

and the same weighted interval DP minimizes this lower bound over the class. This is a generic VC/Rademacher comparator, not a claim that the bound is sharp for interval unions.

Appendix H Experimental details and complete empirical tables

H.1 Matched-family efficiency simulation

We fix B=256B=256, p=.25p=.25, κ=.5\kappa=.5, k∈{1,4,16,64,256}k\in\{1,4,16,64,256\} and γ∈{.04,.02}\gamma\in\{.04,.02\}. The finite sample-size grid for IUT multiplies (.12​k+.9​k+1.5)/γ2(.12k+.9\sqrt{k}+1.5)/\gamma^{2} by .4,.6,.8,1,1.25,1.6,2.4,.6,.8,1,1.25,1.6,2, rounded to multiples of 50; every crossing is bracketed. These grids are computational design choices, not fitted rate claims. Each of the 70 alternative grid points uses 1,500 independent audits. Ten boundary checks, one per (k,γ)(k,\gamma), use the grid point nearest observed 80% power, a boundary-null law and independent randomness, with 20,000 audits each (boundary_all.py). For k=1,4,16,64,256k=1,4,16,64,256 the rejection rates are 4.73, 2.75, 1.44, 0.37 and 0.00% at γ=.04\gamma=.04 and 4.73, 2.59, 1.66, 0.29 and 0.00% at γ=.02\gamma=.02; the largest Wilson upper limit is 5.03%. The alternatives use 105,000 IUT audits in total. Seeds are recorded in the scripts and depend on the configuration.

For the NP envelope, the grid multiplies (.7​k+1)/γ2(.7\sqrt{k}+1)/\gamma^{2} by .5,.7,.9,1.1,1.35,1.65,2.5,.7,.9,1.1,1.35,1.65,2, rounded to multiples of 25. At each of 70 points, 12,000 independent mixture draws calibrate a nominal 5% likelihood-ratio threshold; 6,000 fresh reference draws estimate power and 6,000 fresh mixture draws estimate size. The factorized likelihood ratio is invariant under flipping any group half, so sampling the all-++ feasible component gives the same LR distribution as sampling the uniform component mixture. We test this symmetry directly. Calibration is independent of both evaluations. Pointwise Wilson intervals for the evaluations condition on the calibrated threshold and do not include its calibration uncertainty. The empirical size column is retained; the fitted threshold is not asserted to have exact 5% size. The population NP envelope bounds full-null-valid power, but the estimated curve is descriptive.

For exact computation, subtract the smaller half count in every group from the accepted-count state. The reachable width is then at most 1+∑b|nb,+−nb,−|1+\sum_{b}|n_{b,+}-n_{b,-}|, rather than n+1n+1. A compiled implementation performs the same two-choice recurrence over this interval, with unreachable states at infinity. This compression is exact and is checked against the independent uncompressed dynamic program, including final binomial decisions. Source code and a compiler invocation are supplied; no prebuilt binary is needed.

The recorded constructive-witness fraction selects the half with more correct observations in each heavy group and a fixed half in residual groups. Whenever it has accepted count at least n/2n/2 and empirical risk at most α\alpha, IUT rejection is impossible; the simulation checks this deterministic implication. The theorem does not require this particular witness to be optimal.

H.2 Structured certificate comparison on all frozen outputs

Semi-synthetic power study.

The protocol is described in Section 6. Scripts: semisynthetic_power.py, make_semisyn_table.py, make_semisyn_full.py. Table 8 lists the IUT for every KK and the other certificates at K=4K=4.

Fixed-split frontiers on 12 outputs.

We use one predeclared split, seed 3401, for each of the 12 frozen model outputs. Calibration uses half the scores and no audit labels; audit counts use the disjoint half. We report every combination of K=1,4,16K=1,4,16 at κ=.9\kappa=.9. For each configuration, IUT, policywise Bonferroni, and DKW use the nominal error budget .05.05. The Rademacher calculation uses 200,000 signs for each of the coverage and accepted-error classes; Hoeffding upper confidence corrections cost .0005.0005 each, with the remaining .049.049 allocated over four one-sided data events. Guarantees are pointwise in KK, not simultaneous over all reported configurations. These methods have different inferential targets internally but each resulting frontier is valid for the same existential contract. The global-loss comparator is deliberately described as score-agnostic, and no data-dependent maximum of unadjusted certificates is used.

H.3 Held-out ImageNetV2 IUT audit

For the reference-free certificate, we use the frozen ImageNetV2 ViT-B/16 output and split it 50/50 with seed 3401. The calibration half defines 57 ordered cells from the stored max_softmax_score channel; the audit half contains 5,000 images and supplies all labels/counts. We search unions of at most KK contiguous cell intervals and report the 90%-coverage contract. Alongside the exact IUT we report policywise Bonferroni, the structured DKW comparator of Appendix G.5, and the VC/Rademacher comparator of Appendix G.6.

The IUT value stabilizes once additional intervals no longer improve the relevant frontier. DKW accumulates endpoint error linearly in KK, while the empirical-Rademacher baseline explicitly controls the VC-2​K2K interval-union class without a raw policy-count correction but is still conservative at this sample size. Thus the comparison does not rest on Bonferroni as the only alternative. A one-policy split-sample select-then-test procedure is not listed because it tests only the selected member and is not level-valid for the existential union null. We do not claim any displayed comparator is minimax optimal for the existential problem. On the supplied CPU implementation (M=57,n=5000M=57,n=5000), median DP times are 1.15, 1.60, 2.43, 4.34, 8.13, and 14.80 ms for K=1,2,4,8,16,32K=1,2,4,8,16,32, respectively; absolute timing is environment-specific.

Boundary-null implementation check.

We additionally simulate 1,000 i.i.d. audits from a finite-cell null containing a known boundary witness: 12 equally likely score cells, A∗A^{*} equal to the first nine cells, c⁡(A∗)=.75c(A^{*})=.75, r⁡(A∗)=.20r(A^{*})=.20, K=3K=3, and n=300n=300. The IUT+DP implementation rejects the true null in 9/1,000 runs, an empirical rate of 0.9% with 95% Wilson interval 0.47–1.70%. This is intentionally only an implementation regression check; Proposition 1 supplies the exact finite-sample level guarantee.

Operating-characteristic check.

To distinguish conservativeness at the boundary from lack of power, we keep the same M=12M=12, K=3K=3, n=300n=300, κ=.75\kappa=.75, and target α=.20\alpha=.20 design and vary the best population risk. Over 2,000 simulations per point, rejection rates are:

best population risk .20 .22 .25 .30 .35
IUT rejection rate .0115 .0555 .3015 .8620 .9955

This is a descriptive power curve, not a replacement for Proposition 1’s exact level guarantee. It shows that the 0.9–1.2% boundary rejection rate is a feature of conservative exact one-sided bounds rather than a procedure that remains inert away from the boundary.

Family-flexibility power cost.

The phrase “no multiplicity correction” concerns the level proof, not immunity of power to the size of the searched family. To isolate this distinction, we simulate a homogeneous alternative with M=12M=12, n=300n=300, κ=.75\kappa=.75, target α=.20\alpha=.20, and population risk .25.25 in every score cell. Hence every policy in every interval-union class has exactly the same population risk; increasing KK creates no better population witness. Over 3,000 simulations, IUT rejection falls from 23.1% at K=1K=1 to 7.6% at K=2K=2, 4.7% at K=3K=3, and 4.4% at K=4K=4 and 66. The median lower frontier simultaneously falls from 18.17% to 16.03%. Thus family flexibility can materially reduce power even though the exact type-I argument pays no raw |𝒜||\mathcal{A}| factor.

H.4 Abstention-odds simulation

Design. Scores are uniform over M=64M=64 equal-mass cells and L∼Bern⁡(.14)L\sim\Bern(.14) independently of the score, so every union of cells has risk .14=α+γ.14=\alpha+\gamma with α=.10\alpha=.10, γ=.04\gamma=.04; the law lies in 𝒫γ​(𝒜K)\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}(\mathcal{A}_{K}) for every KK and κ\kappa, and every rule is exactly as bad as every other. On a grid of log-spaced sizes from 150 to 15,846 (the first 15 points of a 19-point grid up to 60,000; the run was stopped once every power had reached 1) we draw 250 audits per size, with seeds 6101 and 6102 for the two interleaved halves of the grid. The normalization divides by the abstention odds and by log⁡(e/min⁡{κ,1−κ})\log(e/\min\{\kappa,1-\kappa\}), a logarithmic factor suggested by localized VC bounds (Appendix B.3); without that logarithm the normalized costs still vary much less than the raw ones (at K=4K=4: 3.9 at κ=.5\kappa=.5 and 9.8 at κ=.95\kappa=.95, against a raw variation of 7.7-fold in the opposite direction). At κ=.3\kappa=.3 the normalized costs are 0.56–0.64 times those at κ=.5\kappa=.5, within the constant factor that separates (1−κ)/κ(1-\kappa)/\kappa from min⁡{κ,1−κ}/κ2\min\{\kappa,1-\kappa\}/\kappa^{2}. At κ≥.9\kappa\geq.9 and K≥8K\geq 8 the crossings stop growing: the abstained region contains only M⁡(1−κ)≤6.4M(1-\kappa)\leq 6.4 cells, so no new rule competes. The constant-risk law is not the least favorable law of Theorem 1; the experiment checks the κ\kappa-dependence of the IUT’s cost, which is governed by the upper bound. Script: kappa_law.py; figure and table: make_kappa_figure.py, make_kappa_table.py.

H.5 A valid non-EFC audit: cross-fit universal inference

Identify each law with its pushforward to the 2​M2M cell-by-loss categories; as in Appendix B.2, this loses nothing for the null because every rule is a union of cells. For A∈𝒜A\in\mathcal{A} let ℋA\mathcal{H}_{A} be the laws under which AA meets the contract, so ℋ=⋃AℋA\mathcal{H}=\bigcup_{A}\mathcal{H}_{A}.

Lemma 4 (Profile likelihood of the existential null).

Let xx be category counts with total n0n_{0}, and let c^\hat{c} be the empirical coverage of AA. When c^>0\hat{c}>0, let r^\hat{r} be its empirical risk; when c^=0\hat{c}=0, define the product c^ 1{r^>α}kl(r^,α)\hat{c}\,\mathbf{1}\{\hat{r}>\alpha\}\,\mathrm{kl}(\hat{r},\alpha) below to be zero. Then

supQ∈ℋA∑ixilogQi=∑ixilogxin0−n0[𝟏{c^<κ}kl(c^,κ)+c^ 1{r^>α}kl(r^,α)].\sup_{Q\in\mathcal{H}_{A}}\sum_{i}x_{i}\log Q_{i}=\sum_{i}x_{i}\log\frac{x_{i}}{n_{0}}-n_{0}\Big[\mathbf{1}\{\hat{c}<\kappa\}\,\mathrm{kl}(\hat{c},\kappa)+\hat{c}\,\mathbf{1}\{\hat{r}>\alpha\}\,\mathrm{kl}(\hat{r},\alpha)\Big].
Proof.

The constraints of ℋA\mathcal{H}_{A} involve QQ only through the four masses Q⁡(A,0),Q⁡(A,1),Q⁡(Ac,0),Q⁡(Ac,1)Q(A,0),Q(A,1),Q(A^{c},0),Q(A^{c},1). For fixed masses, the likelihood is maximized by splitting each mass in proportion to the counts, which gives ∑ixilog(xi/n0)−n0KL(p^∥Q4)\sum_{i}x_{i}\log(x_{i}/n_{0})-n_{0}\,\KL(\hat{p}\|Q_{4}), where p^\hat{p} and Q4Q_{4} are the empirical and model four-cell laws. Parametrize Q4Q_{4} by c=Q⁡(A)c=Q(A), r=Q⁡(L=1∣A)r=Q(L=1\mid A) and s=Q⁡(L=1∣Ac)s=Q(L=1\mid A^{c}). The chain rule gives KL(p^∥Q4)=kl(c^,c)+c^kl(r^,r)+(1−c^)kl(s^,s)\KL(\hat{p}\|Q_{4})=\mathrm{kl}(\hat{c},c)+\hat{c}\,\mathrm{kl}(\hat{r},r)+(1-\hat{c})\mathrm{kl}(\hat{s},s), with zero-weight conditional terms defined as zero (so the empirical conditional proportion on an empty block may be chosen arbitrarily). The constraints are c≥κc\geq\kappa and r≤αr\leq\alpha, and the three terms are minimized separately by c=max⁡{c^,κ}c=\max\{\hat{c},\kappa\}, by r=min⁡{r^,α}r=\min\{\hat{r},\alpha\} when c^>0\hat{c}>0, and by s=s^s=\hat{s} when c^<1\hat{c}<1; the corresponding zero-weight choices are immaterial. ∎

For t>0t>0, the bracket is increasing in the error count for a fixed accepted count, so the minimal error counts eK​(t)e_{K}(t) of the interval dynamic program (Appendix G) suffice. If a nonempty frozen score cell receives zero observations in the evaluated split, a nonempty rule with t=0t=0 is also available and contributes the coverage-only penalty kl⁡(0,κ)\mathrm{kl}(0,\kappa); we include this candidate explicitly. The structurally empty mask is not a witness for the existential null. On small instances the formula agrees with numerical constrained optimization to 10−910^{-9}, and the dynamic-program minimum, including the zero-count edge case, agrees with brute-force enumeration.

The audit. Split the audit sample into halves D0,D1D_{0},D_{1}. Let P^1\hat{P}_{1} be the add-1/21/2 smoothed empirical law of D1D_{1} over the 2​M2M categories, Λ0=P^1n0​(D0)/supQ∈ℋQn0​(D0)\Lambda_{0}=\hat{P}_{1}^{n_{0}}(D_{0})/\sup_{Q\in\mathcal{H}}Q^{n_{0}}(D_{0}) the split likelihood ratio, Λ1\Lambda_{1} its mirror image, and reject when (Λ0+Λ1)/2≥1/δ(\Lambda_{0}+\Lambda_{1})/2\geq 1/\delta. For every Q∈ℋQ\in\mathcal{H}, 𝔼Q​[Λ0∣D1]≤𝔼Q​[P^1n0​(D0)/Qn0​(D0)∣D1]≤1\mathbb{E}_{Q}[\Lambda_{0}\mid D_{1}]\leq\mathbb{E}_{Q}[\hat{P}_{1}^{n_{0}}(D_{0})/Q^{n_{0}}(D_{0})\mid D_{1}]\leq 1: explicitly, the latter expectation sums P^1n0\hat{P}_{1}^{n_{0}} only over sample sequences with positive Qn0Q^{n_{0}} mass, and equals one when P^1≪Q\hat{P}_{1}\ll Q. The same holds for Λ1\Lambda_{1}, so the average is an e-value and Markov’s inequality gives level δ\delta over the unrestricted null (Wasserman et al., 2020). The audit is not EFC: it may reject although a rule is empirically feasible on the full sample. It is a natural reference-free competitor, and it is not the testing-scale audit of Theorem 4, which requires constant risk.

Results. Table 12 compares it with the IUT on the same draws. No boundary rejection was observed for the universal-inference audit. The IUT’s largest boundary rejection rate in these runs is 4.0% (ImageNetV2, K=1K=1, n=50,000n=50{,}000, 200 audits), within Monte Carlo error of its exact level; up to n=20,000n=20{,}000 it matches the at most 1.8% of Table 8 within that error. The χ2\chi^{2} independence test rejected in all 200 audits at n=500n=500 on every population. The numerator must fit the full cell-by-loss law, which has up to 2​M−1=1132M-1=113 free parameters here (105 for CIFAR-10 after ties are merged); this is a substantial finite-sample burden that the IUT does not incur. Script: nonefc_semisyn.py; table: make_nonefc_table.py.

Appendix I Artifact provenance and automated checks

The release includes the frozen dependency artifact plus an analysis directory containing the operational benchmark, sign-family simulation, full-null window reconstruction, exact parity certificates, validation tests, and generated manuscript tables. All computational configurations have recorded deterministic seeds. Figures and numerical controls computed from frozen outputs are identified as such; their source scripts and input arrays are included. The parity certificates are verified with rational arithmetic; the sign dynamic program and binomial rejection lookup are checked against independent exhaustive calculations; singleton radii are checked against constrained four-cell numerical optimization. The release README supplies commands, software versions, and claim-to-file mappings.
